title: Facing Reality
summary: After claiming her old report, contact 030 mentions how things are going in this exchange. Report 89's main text is not included.

frames.label: Note
frames.text:
Source: correspondence between the handler and contact 030.
Report 89's main text is not included; only what was actually said in this exchange is arranged below, with identifying details removed.
Let me claim it. A report I wrote a long time ago, number 89.

frames.name: Handler
frames.text: Mm. I'm listening.
It was very short back then. A lot went unsaid.
Several friends died.

frames.name: Handler
frames.text: Mm.
Later I met my boyfriend in an od group.

frames.name: Handler
frames.text: In a group too.
Mm. Everything's good, except the long distance.

frames.name: Handler
frames.text: Still using?
Quitting O.

frames.name: Handler
frames.text: How's it going?
Chronic opioid dependence. Not so easy to cut.

frames.name: Handler
frames.text: Then take it slow.
I've met his parents.
After that we're thinking of moving, and getting married.

frames.name: Handler
frames.text: Sounds like a good thing.
It is. It's just not decided yet.

frames.name: Handler
frames.text: So would that count as coming down off the plateau?
Off the plateau. I've got to shore.

frames.name: Handler
frames.text: And now?
Over a year without self-harm. The depression's much better too.
Does that count as the od circle's hidden ending?

frames.name: Handler
frames.text: No.

frames.name: Handler
frames.text: You just faced reality.
Facing reality... sounds worse than hidden ending.

frames.name: Handler
frames.text: But it's true.
Mm. Friends are gone, the dependence is still there, moving and marriage still not decided.
Anything else, this and that, I won't write.

frames.name: Handler
frames.text: Mm. That's enough.

frames.label: Handler's Note
frames.text:
Report 89 is only a few pages and its main text isn't collected here.
This piece isn't a sequel to it, and doesn't treat her later life as proof of a cure.
She just got to shore, carrying dead friends, chronic dependence and a long-distance life.
Facing reality isn't clearing the game; it's admitting all this and still walking on.
She didn't write her specific prescriptions, her friends' names or the wedding date here; and this piece won't fill them in for her.

frames.label: Archive
frames.text: Not entered into the report series / kept only as contact correspondence.
